lines.trans: Well, of course.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ынок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'son' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Лёша, что случилось? Дыши, сынок, дыши!
examples.trans: Lyosha, what happened? Breathe, son, breathe!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hi', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'fridge' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The milk is in the fridge.

examples.text: Курица? Нет. А чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'socks' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты обещал мне носки не разбрасывать.
examples.trans: You promised me not to scatter your socks.

examples.text: Носки я уже совсем не разбрасываю.
examples.trans: I do not scatter my socks anymore at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'put on', paired with 'надевать'.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

examples.text: Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

examples.text: Что, я зря пришла? Я надела костюм зайки!
examples.trans: What, did I come for nothing? I put on a bunny costume!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('warm').

examples.trans: And where are your warm gloves?

examples.text: Да, его тёплая шапка лежит прямо здесь.
examples.trans: Yes, his warm hat is lying right here.

examples.text: Снимайте скорее с него тёплые валенки.
examples.trans: Take off his warm felt boots quickly.

examples.text: Нужно класть в стакан больше льда.
examples.trans: You need to put more ice into the glass.

examples.text: Лидия Алексеевна, успокойтесь, пожалуйста! Вы как маленькая себя ведёте.
examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.
You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.text: Вы ведёте себя как подросток! Вы приударяете за мной.
examples.trans: You are behaving like a teenager! You are flirting with me.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.
